analysis.title: Huang-Over: Stocks Jump, Oil Dumps After Weekend Of 'Fear And Loathing'
key_insights: Stocks rebounded sharply on Nov 10, 2026 from overnight lows in a short squeeze, after positioning and leverage hit washed-out lows and panic indicators spiked. DOW, SPX and RTY erased their post-election losses. NDX and RTY gained over 3.5%.
NVDA fell 4.5% after news of an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. NVDA is down year to date, and its loss was AMD's gain. Mag7 rose about 1% against about 3% for the SPX ex-Mag7 (SPX 493).

Oil fell more than 4% to six-week lows (WTI in the $85 range). Drivers were Trump calling extensive strikes on Iran 'highly unlikely' and a late Al Arabiya report that arrangements are being made to discuss the return of IAEA inspectors to Iran. Brent returned to last week's lows.

Money managers had already cut bullish crude bets. Net-long Brent was the lowest since early August and WTI longs the smallest since early July, which left crude exposed to an unwind on positive geopolitical news.

Oil is still up more than 50% this year. OPEC output last month rose to 88% of prewar volumes (Bloomberg survey). Iranian output has fallen under a US naval blockade. A tanker was reportedly hit near the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi rebels damaged Aramco offices in Riyadh.
Supertanker rates from the US Gulf to Asia fell to $45 million from $79.6 million a month ago, but remain historically elevated.

US natural gas rose on cooler Atlantic seaboard forecasts, amplified by short covering. European TTF gas fell on Iran peace-talk hopes. European storage is 73% full against a five-year norm of 89%, and the deficit may persist into 2027.

Treasuries sold off across the curve as appetite for stocks and corporates recovered, with the short end underperforming. Rate-hike expectations rose after a sticky NY Fed October consumer inflation survey and non-dovish remarks from Goolsbee and Barkin.
Heavy Treasury supply: $58B 3-year notes on Nov 10, $42B 10-year notes on Nov 11 and $25B 30-year bonds on Nov 12, front-loaded because of the Veterans Day bond market holiday. The curve flattened.
Dealers said last week's yields reached levels unlikely to be breached without new threats. Abate and Gandhi wrote that a sustained break may need clearer evidence of weaker growth.
Credit tightened. IG spreads narrowed and hyperscaler credit risk returned near one-month lows. Data-center CDS fell back below 500bps. Chipmaker credit risk is now above hyperscaler credit risk.

Goldman's Kevin Boova said credit showed no signs of panic. IG outperformed last week while NDX fell almost 5%, SPX 2.7% and VIX topped 25, and ORCL, META and AAPL financings cleared. He said AI capex financing cannot assume unlimited capital, and that crowding out is becoming real and favors the highest-quality names.
CoreWeave (CRWV) reports earnings on Nov 11 with its bonds trading above 1200bps.

UBS said Nov 5 capitulation signals, strong real-money support and very low hedge fund and systematic positioning make for an asymmetric upside setup. Morgan Stanley and RBC strategists say the correction may be entering its final phase, with year-end rally potential.
Goldman's Lee Coppersmith said near-term tails remain unusually large and more positioning remains to be worked through, though panic readings at extremes make the setup more interesting.
Nasdaq reversed lower at its 200-day moving average. VIX fell back to about 20. Goldman's Panic Index had a record two-day surge before the bounce.

Goldman's desk saw light activity on the snapback, with investors preferring to buy a breakout. Flows were 3% better to buy. CTAs sold a lot of S&P, buybacks are back, and levered ETF volumes (SOXL and SOXS) hit records last week. Semis showed a second day of buy skew ex-NVDA, and last week's global tech selling matched the largest on record per prime brokerage.
The realized volatility of VVIX hit an all-time high over 5 and 10 days (Coppersmith). VVIX then fell, its third-largest drop in 20 years.
Anthropic is reported to launch marketing of its Nasdaq IPO on Tuesday (IFR).
The dollar returned to pre-election levels. Gold held around $4,100. Bitcoin fell to $73,500 on Nov 9 evening and bounced on Nov 10 but is still lower since Friday's equity close.

Bloomberg's Frank Monkam said the Huang investigation adds governance, key-person and possible national-security risk. NVDA is 7% of SPX weight and about 25% of its variance. He sees the market's rebound as mechanical dip-buying that dismisses these risks.
Goldman models show $25B or more of potential CTA supply this week. CPI and CoreWeave earnings, both due Nov 11, are possible catalysts.

market_movers.rationale: Shares fell 4.5% on news of an investigation into CEO Jensen Huang. Bloomberg's Monkam flags governance, key-person and national-security risk. NVDA is about 7% of SPX weight and 25% of its variance.
AMD gained as NVDA lost, per the note's chart commentary.
Earnings due Nov 11 with bond spreads holding above 1200bps.

sector_views.rationale: Goldman's Boova remains constructive on high-quality credit, expecting AI financing to favor the largest, highest-rated names. He sees few cracks in financing for the non-AI world.
Energy stocks turned negative late as oil fell. TD Securities' McKay says deal talk suppresses upside, but further material downside should be limited without a concrete deal.
Tech and industrials outperformed on the day. Optical networking and data-center stocks outperformed, neoclouds less so. Semis show buy skew ex-NVDA.

earnings_insights: CoreWeave (CRWV) reports on Nov 11, 2026 (expectation, not a print). Its bond spreads were above 1200bps.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Late IAEA headline pushed crude lower after positioning had already been trimmed.
War has hampered Middle East flows, but futures are increasingly sensitive to bearish geopolitical news.
Persian Gulf exports have picked up (Bloomberg survey).
Supply remains strained and the deficit may last into 2027.
The short end led the selloff on sticky inflation data and hawkish Fed speakers.

macro_indicators.reading: sticky inflation expectations, well above the Fed's 2% target
macro_indicators.interpretation: Pressures the front end and lifts rate-hike expectations.
Bounced Nov 10 but remains below Friday's equity close level.
VIX fell back from above 25 last week.

crypto_views: Bitcoin fell to $73,500 on Nov 9 evening after a large drop the prior Thursday, then bounced on Nov 10 but remained below Friday's equity close level. Bitcoin volatility spiked while the dollar dipped.
risk_factors: Nvidia investigation: governance, key-person and national-security risk that could linger for months.
Liquidity deteriorating, positioning impaired and volatility in the upper end of its range, so capacity to absorb a shock is constrained.
Possible $25B or more of CTA supply this week.
AI capex financing and crowding out. Lower-quality borrowers may lose market access.
Middle East flare-ups (Hormuz tanker incident, Houthi attack on Aramco) could reverse oil's decline.
Hawkish Fed speakers and sticky inflation expectations raising rate-hike pricing.
Heavy Treasury auction calendar adding concession pressure.
The panic-buying pattern has appeared recently and failed before.
vol_and_positioning: VIX fell back to about 20 from above 25 last week.
VVIX realized volatility hit an all-time high over 5 and 10 days, then VVIX dropped its third-most in 20 years (Coppersmith).
Goldman's Panic Index had a record two-day surge before the bounce. Positioning and leverage were at washed-out lows.
Levered ETF participation hit records last week (SOXL and SOXS record volume days).
CTAs sold a lot of S&P. Goldman models show $25B or more of potential CTA supply this week.
Money managers' net-long Brent is the lowest since early August and WTI longs the smallest since early July.
Hedge fund shorts were squeezed for a second day. 'Check Receivers' outperformed 'Check Writers' for a second day.
geopolitical: US-Iran war: Trump said it is 'highly unlikely' he will order extensive strikes on Iran, and the Democratic midterm sweep adds pressure to seek an off-ramp.
Al Arabiya sources report arrangements to discuss the return of IAEA inspectors to Iran, with the scope of their duties unclear.

US naval blockade on Iranian exports continues. A tanker was reportedly hit by an unknown projectile near the Strait of Hormuz (UKMTO), and Houthi rebels damaged Saudi Aramco offices in Riyadh, prompting Saudi retaliation against two missile launchers.
Investigation into Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang with possible national-security implications (Bloomberg's Monkam).

tension_points.bull_case: Trump signals no appetite for escalation, IAEA inspector talks are being arranged, and speculative longs have been trimmed. TD's McKay says deal talk will suppress upside.
